Definition: from G1173; to dine, i.e. take the principle (or evening) meal:--sup (X -er).
BiblicalUsage: To sup is to sit at the table for the evening meal, and the word gathers the suppers of the Gospels: the master who bids his servant to make ready and serve him, the Lord who sups with the one who opens the door, and the cup of the new testament in His blood. Supper is fellowship, and the Lord's Supper is the fellowship that remembers Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the table is where the Lord meets His people: He who was betrayed at supper still invites us to sup with Him. The supper is the fellowship that remains when the crowds have gone, and the Lord still sets the table.
